speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started in relation to your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically involving the Auriculotemporal branch) secondary to post-surgical neuralgia from your tympanoplasty.

The "shooting pain when eating" suggests a trigger zone in your V3 branch, and the discomfort with earrings points to V2/V3 involvement near the ear. Given your history of chronic ear infections and recent surgery, this is likely post-surgical neuralgia rather than a recurrent infection or hardware issue. Do you experience any numbness in your face or jaw, or does the pain ever radiate to your teeth or tongue?
